summary: Reify clause-level reason/purpose (have-reason-91/have-purpose-91); split verb+量/率/额 compounds and use have-quant-91 for amounts reached; bare-verb frame for V至/V到 tokens; widen Chinese ARG0-theme warning; narrow shared-subject re-entrancy, head-noun/appositive/旗下 rules; individual-person, middle-dot op, agent nouns; fix temporal rules for absolute dates, purpose, cause/earlier relatives, depends-on, decade; aspect/modal/coref details.

edits.old: *because* (因为) → `:cause`; 由于 and the frame 以…而 → `:reason`;
edits.new: *because* (因为) → `:cause` (phrasal); 由于 and the frame 以…而 → `:reason` (phrasal);

edits.text: - **Clause-linking reason and purpose (overrides the phrasal rules above).** When a reason connective (因为…于是/所以, 由于…, 所以) or a purpose connective (为/为了 + a clause) links two full clauses, reify it: `(h / have-reason-91 :ARG1 effect-event :ARG2 cause-event :aspect state)`, `(h2 / have-purpose-91 :ARG1 main-event :ARG2 purpose-event :aspect state)`. The reified node is the root, or sits above the main event. It gets `(author :full-affirmative h)` but no temporal parent (see 5.1). Keep `:cause` / `:reason` / `:purpose` only when the cause or purpose is a phrase, not a full clause.

edits.old: Use a shorter form or `-00` only if the whole token has no frame.
edits.new: Use a shorter form or `-00` only if the whole token has no frame. If a verb + complement token (V至, V到, V为, V成) has no frame, use the bare verb's frame; the endpoint fills that frame's end-point role (or comes through `have-quant-91`, 2.2). Never use a concept whose word is not a PropBank lemma unless it is `-00`.

edits.anchor: Do not default the theme to `:ARG1` by English habit.
edits.text: In particular, for change, become, reach and fall verbs (成, 达到, 跌, 变 type), the theme is usually `:ARG0` and the result or point reached is `:ARG1`. Copy the numbers from the roleset's role list every time.

**Measure compounds.** A Chinese noun made of a verb + 量 / 率 / 额 (the quantity, rate or amount of V-ing) is split. The measure morpheme is the head, `(q / 量 :quant-of (e / V-01 :ARG1 ...))`. The verb is a real event (aspect, temporal `:overlap` with its governing verb, modal link), and its own arguments (the owner, etc.) attach to the verb, not as `:possessor`. **Amounts reached.** A number reached, fallen to or amounting to (达到 N, 跌至 N, 为 N) goes on the measured noun as `(q :ARG1-of (h / have-quant-91 :ARG2 N :unit (u / <classifier>)))`. Do not create a separate `thing :quant N`.

- A named human is `individual-person`, not `person`. `person` stays for pronouns and unnamed people.
- The middle dot `·` in a transliterated foreign name is its own `:op`.

A compound agent noun (V + 人/者, e.g. a founder or initiator) is decomposed: `(p / 人 :ARG0-of (v / V-01 :aspect performance))`, placed where the role noun goes (e.g. under `:ARG3` of the role predicate).

edits.old: A subject shared through a control, serial or purpose/means frame (以 X 而 Y, *known for doing X*, *try to X*) counts as expressed: re-enter it as the subject of the embedded verb too.
edits.new: A subject grammatically shared through a control or means frame (以 X 而 Y, *known for doing X*, *try to X*) counts as expressed: re-enter it as the subject of the embedded verb too. Do not re-enter the subject into 为/为了-purpose clauses or into relative clauses; leave those roles out unless a word fills them.

edits.anchor: A medium noun (TV, 网络) modifying a program or product is `:medium`.
edits.text:
- **Heads.** In N1 的 N2, and in *change from A to B* (从 A 变为 B), the grammatical head common noun is the concept. A publication or organization name modifying it is `:part-of` (a part, section or edition of it) or `:possessor`, not the head.
- **Appositives.** An appositive descriptor before or after a name (its 旗下 tabloid 《X》) is `(x / <type> :name ... :ARG1-of (i / identity-91 :ARG2 (d / <descriptor> :mod ...)))`. Words like 旗下 stay a `:mod` node on the descriptor; do not turn them into a `:possessor` edge.
A decade expression (X年代) is written with `:era`, not `:decade`.

(see below)
- **Purpose verbs** naming an ongoing use are `activity`. A relative-clause verb giving what something is for or contains is `process`. A manner or property word on an event nominal is `:manner`, not `:mod`.
- **Stative verbs, continued.**

edits.new: a past absolute date (*1998*) is `(document-creation-time :before date)` (a future one `:after`);

edits.old: (1) to a time expression of its clause, if there is one (`(s1t :contained s1e)`);
edits.new: (1) to a time expression of its clause, if there is one (`(s1t :overlap s1e)`);

edits.old: Use `:overlap` unless the order is explicit (`:before`/`:after`; a purpose is `:after` its main event).
edits.new: Use `:overlap` unless the order is explicit (`:before`/`:after`). A purpose clause is `:overlap` its main event. A cause clause, and a relative clause describing an earlier event (left over, previously ...), is `:before` its parent, even when it is marked future (将) relative to its own time.

edits.old: - A completed event whose result describes the present situation (a status reached, a name or evaluation given: a naming/evaluation passive, 已经 + a completed change) is linked as `(document-creation-time :depends-on e)`.
edits.new: - A naming or evaluation passive (被称为, 被誉为) whose result describes the present is linked as `(document-creation-time :depends-on e)`. Use this only for naming and evaluation. A narrative change (成了, became) that continues an earlier sentence's story takes that earlier event as its reference time (`:overlap` or `:after`).

edits.old: - Every event node must get exactly one temporal parent. Two exceptions:
edits.new: - Every event node must get exactly one temporal parent. Exceptions (also: `have-reason-91` and `have-purpose-91` get no temporal parent, but their argument events do):

edits.old:
Purpose and condition clauses may use the
  constants `purpose` and `have-condition` as parents of their events.
edits.new:
Purpose and condition clauses may use the
  constants `purpose` and `have-condition` as parents of their events. A purpose event that the text shows is actually realized is `(author :full-affirmative e)`.

edits.old: - `(earlier :same-event later)`: two mentions of the same event.
edits.new: - `(earlier :same-event later)`: two mentions of the very same event (the same act mentioned again). Do not link two different events that are merely related (e.g. a thing's founding and a later act by its founder).
